decisions.status: RULED 22 Aug 2026 — merged at v6
decisions.title: The three city foreign keys are ON DELETE RESTRICT
decisions.evidence: `places.city_id`, `photos.city_id` and `walks.city_id` had no settled delete action, and the reason is benign rather than an oversight: THE CLIENT HAS NO DELETE-A-CITY CONTROL, so no sheet copy exists to derive one from. Every other cascade in this schema is read off a sentence the user is shown; these three had no sentence. The Phase 1 class diagram drew them UNSETTLED and flagged them, which is how the question surfaced.
decisions.reasoning:
Three arguments, in order of weight.
(1) THE FAILURE MODES ARE NOT SYMMETRIC. RESTRICT -> CASCADE later is a one-line migration. CASCADE -> RESTRICT *after* it has silently destroyed photographs is not a migration at all — there is nothing to migrate back to. When the answer is genuinely unknown, take the reversible one.
(2) A CASCADE HERE WOULD BE THE LARGEST DESTRUCTIVE ACT IN THE APP — every place in the city, every photograph taken there across every trip, every walk — and it would fire from a control that does not exist, silently. Compare what the app demands for something far smaller: D3 itemises four consequences and makes the user type the trip's name out. THE GOVERNING CONVENTION OF THIS SCHEMA IS THAT A CASCADE DOES EXACTLY WHAT ITS SHEET SAYS. Here there is no sheet, so nothing authorises it.
(3) IT SURFACES THE MISSING DECISION AT THE RIGHT MOMENT. Whoever adds a delete-a-city control is stopped by the database precisely when they are in a position to write the confirmation copy.
AND IT EXTENDS AN INSTINCT THE PLAN ALREADY HAS RATHER THAN INTRODUCING ONE: deleting a trip already KEEPS its places and KEEPS its cities — 'the pins stay in those cities' — so refusing to let a city vanish underneath them is the same posture one level up.
decisions.consequence:
Three FKs at `ON DELETE RESTRICT` in migration 0001, EACH CARRYING A COMMENT SAYING IT IS RESTRICTIVE BECAUSE NO USER-FACING SENTENCE AUTHORISES A CASCADE — so the next reader knows it is a decision and not a default, which is the same reason every other FK in that file quotes its sheet line. `RESTRICT` rather than `NO ACTION`: it checks immediately rather than at constraint-check time, and it states the intent.
THE FK COUNT MOVES FROM SEVEN TO TEN and S06's acceptance check is re-derived rather than incremented — seven derived from sheet copy, plus these three derived from the ABSENCE of sheet copy, plus the one deliberate no-FK (trips->places). It also removes UNSETTLED from the Phase 1 diagram's relationship table.
TRIGGER FOR REVISITING: a delete-a-city control. At that point the sheet copy is written FIRST and the FK follows it, which is the order every other cascade in this app was decided in.

steps.title: Object storage: the config seam, and minio-go behind one interface
steps.size: LARGE — and its deliverable changed shape at v4: a thin wrapper, not a signer
steps.work:
THE CONFIG SEAM FIRST AND IN THIS COMMIT (DEC-42): `S3_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` (what the CLIENT reaches media at — THE SIGNER TAKES THIS ONE, because a presigned signature covers the host and no proxy can rewrite it afterwards), `S3_INTERNAL_ENDPOINT` (what the API uses for HEAD and DELETE inside the network; defaults to the public one), plus bucket, region, credentials and the two TTLs. No hardcoded fallback.

THEN `objects.Store` — PresignGet, PresignPut, Head, Delete — with ONE minio-go implementation (DEC-43) and one in-memory implementation for handler tests.

*** THE ONE LINE THAT MUST NOT BE WRITTEN WRONG (V3-B1). *** Use `PresignHeader(ctx, http.MethodPut, bucket, key, ttl, nil, http.Header{...})` with `x-amz-checksum-sha256`, `content-length` and `content-type` in the header map, so they land in `X-Amz-SignedHeaders` and THE STORAGE LAYER enforces them. `PresignedPutObject` passes `nil` extra headers (api-presigned.go:90) and so DEC-38's central security claim — 'the server must not trust the client's hash' — evaporates the moment a worker reaches for the obvious call. IT FAILS OPEN: the upload succeeds, the commit HEAD succeeds because the SIZE matches, and the object at address sha256(X) contains Y, after which every `immutable` header and every `alreadyExists: true` is a lie about bytes nobody verified. MEASURED IN v4 AND NOT IN THE CRITIQUE: `Presign` (api-presigned.go:113) ALSO passes nil extra headers, so it is a SECOND fail-open door with a more inviting name. Both are banned.

`response-cache-control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` and `response-content-disposition: attachment` are set on the presigned GET (DEC-38, DEC-51). `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` IS NOT AND CANNOT BE (V4-SF3): S3's response-header override set is closed and nosniff is not in it, minio-go does not validate reqParams so an invented `response-x-...` would be signed and surface as a 400 or a silently absent header, and a leg asserting it could never pass — a v4 fix that introduced an unimplementable requirement — the presigned GET is the only mechanism that does not depend on what the uploader happened to send.

TWO ENCODINGS OF ONE DIGEST, IN THE LINE THAT MUST NOT BE WRITTEN WRONG (V4-SF4): the object id and the bucket key carry the digest as **hex** (64 chars); the signed `x-amz-checksum-sha256` value is the **base64** of the same raw 32 bytes (44 chars). Convert at the presign call. This fails CLOSED — every upload rejected — so it is not the fail-open class, but it lands in the one line the plan flags as unforgiving.

DELETED AT v5 (over-engineered #2): `PresignGetBatch`. Presigning is a local HMAC with no network call, so a batch method saves nothing a loop in the handler does not, while adding a method to the interface and both implementations and a second place for the TTL choice to diverge from `PresignGet`'s. The batch ROUTE is worth having; the batch STORE METHOD is not.

AND DEC-42's SEAM CHECK IS REWRITTEN, BECAUSE THE SWAP BROKE IT (V3-B2). v3 asserted `grep -rniE 'minio|9000|https?://' internal/objects/` returns nothing — which now matches `internal/objects/minio.go`'s OWN IMPORT LINE and false-reds forever against correct code. REPLACED BY an AST check: no string literal reaches the objects constructor except from `internal/config`. State the mechanism, because a grep that cannot pass is worse than no check.

steps.title: The three media routes, the seeded sample images, and the SERVER fixture
steps.size: LARGE — it grew at v4: three routes, the begin-upsert, the media validation, the seeding, and the server fixture
steps.work:
THREE ROUTES: `POST /v1/media` (begin), `POST /v1/media/{id}/commit`, and `POST /v1/media/mint` taking a LIST of ids so a twelve-photo grid is ONE round trip rather than twelve. THE SINGULAR `GET /v1/media/{id}` IS DELETED (over-engineered #1) — it is the batch with a one-element list, and it cost a second handler, a second set of `no-store` legs, a second route-coverage entry and a second place to get the private-vs-public TTL wrong.

BEGIN MUST UPSERT (V3-B5): `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (traveller_id, id) DO UPDATE SET byte_size = EXCLUDED.byte_size WHERE media_objects.uploaded_at IS NULL`, inside `WithTravellerLock` — the WHERE guard added at v5 (V4-SF5b) so a re-begin with a false `byteSize` cannot rewrite the recorded size of an object whose bytes cannot change, and the `RETURNING (xmax = 0)` projection DELETED (over-engineered #4) because nothing consumed it (DEC-50 — media is not in the logbook payload, so it takes the lock and does NOT bump the counter). A SELECT-then-INSERT loses the race between a retry and its own original, which is exactly the retry content addressing exists to make free. `alreadyExists` is derived from `uploaded_at IS NOT NULL`, NOT from row presence, or a begin that never uploaded reports true, the client skips an upload that never happened, and commit 409s with no way forward.

VALIDATION (DEC-51): `contentTypeRe = ^image/(jpeg|png|heic)$` -> 422 invalid_field; `byteSize` bounded by `MEDIA_MAX_BYTES`; both signed into the presigned PUT so the BUCKET enforces them. Capability responses carry `Cache-Control: no-store, private` and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`.

`make seed-media` uploads the two bundled sample PNGs THROUGH THE REAL ROUTES — begin, presigned PUT, commit — so seeding exercises the flow rather than side-loading into the bucket. THEN THE SERVER FIXTURE (DEC-52): `server_log.json`, the client's shape with `asset` and all three `coverAsset` fields rewritten to the two seeded sha256 ids. It is built HERE because this is where those ids come into existence, and S13, S19 and the smoke arc all use it. `-sweep-media`: delete objects unreferenced by ANY of the FOUR asset columns (DEC-46) and older than 24 hours. No scheduler.

AND BEGIN MUST NOT HAND OUT A WRITE CAPABILITY FOR A COMMITTED OBJECT (V4-SF5a): when `alreadyExists` is true the response OMITS `uploadUrl` entirely. DEC-24 already made this exact call for the public envelope — 'no URL is minted at all, not an unusable one, not an expired one' — and handing out a live write URL against an object being served `immutable` is worse than a merely redundant one.
steps.acceptance_check: Uploading the same bytes twice returns `alreadyExists: true` the second time and performs no second upload. Commit without an upload answers `409 upload_incomplete`. A `text/html` contentType is refused. A `byteSize` over `MEDIA_MAX_BYTES` is refused. TWO CONCURRENT BEGINS for the same digest both succeed and produce one row — the leg that catches the missing upsert. AND when `alreadyExists` is true the `uploadUrl` key is ABSENT from the response, not empty.
steps.verified_by: THE END-TO-END LEG: begin -> presigned PUT -> commit -> `PUT /v1/photos/{id}` with that asset -> `POST /v1/media/mint` with that one id -> fetch the returned URL -> bytes match. THE SHARED-OBJECT LEG: two photos referencing one object both survive the deletion of either, and the sweep does not remove it while one remains. THE COVER LEG (DEC-46): an object referenced ONLY by a `coverAsset` survives the sweep — mutation proof narrows the liveness query back to `photos.asset` and it reddens, which is the V3-B6 defect made visible. THE GRACE LEG: an object committed seconds ago and not yet attached survives.

steps.title: THE READ PATH — snapshot, whole-log document, ETag and 304
steps.size: LARGE, and it is v3's centre of gravity
steps.work:
The two transaction helpers landed in S08 (DEC-50); this step adds `read_tx.go` only. read_tx.go: `WithReadSnapshot` at `sql.LevelRepeatableRead`, AND THE VERSION IS READ INSIDE THAT SNAPSHOT — otherwise the phone caches a body under a version that does not describe it, which is the one cache bug that never self-corrects. logbook_read.go assembles the document, which is FIVE LISTS AND ONE OBJECT — `{trips, cities, places, photos, walks, traveller}` — visits nested, `ORDER BY ordinal`. `traveller` was named nowhere in v4 (V4-SF2) though it is presupposed everywhere: DEC-50 lists it as bumping the counter, DEC-24 puts it in the public NEVER list, and `PATCH /v1/me` is one of the 18 writes. Omit it and U1's name silently disappears on every refresh while `setTravellerName` writes a value that never comes back. A registered traveller with no name emits `traveller: null`, NEVER `{"name": ""}` — the client's generated codec casts `json['name'] as String`, non-nullable, so an empty object throws. routes.go declares the `[]Route` slice and registers the mux from it. The handler: read the version FIRST — one indexed SELECT — and if `If-None-Match` matches, return 304 WITHOUT ASSEMBLING THE DOCUMENT. Emits `"version": 2` (DEC-40) from one emitter taking the version as a parameter. `shareLinkId` round-trips from the live share_links row.

ADDED IN v4: the ETag is `W/"<emitterVersion>-<logbookVersion>"` (DEC-49). `emitterVersion` is a Go constant sitting immediately above the emitter with a comment saying what it is for, bumped BY HAND whenever the emitted shape changes — and DEC-40's move to `"version": 2` is its first bump, which is the worked example. Without it a DEPLOY that changes the document never invalidates a cached phone, which holds the old shape and gets 304 forever until somebody happens to write. The write path also SELECTs the ETag INSIDE the bump transaction (V3-B10), so a returned ETag can never describe a state later than the body it came with. And `X-Logbook-Format` is honoured with `406 unsupported_format` (DEC-53).
steps.acceptance_check: An AST walk over `*sql.DB` call expressions catching BOTH `BeginTx` and `Begin`, against the allowlist {tx.go, read_tx.go, migrate.go}. The golden key file matches the emitted bytes and includes `shareLinkId` as a real value.
steps.verified_by:
THE CACHE LEGS. (1) 200 carries an ETag containing the emitter constant — asserted on the constant, so it cannot be quietly dropped. (2) If-None-Match returns 304 AND AN EMPTY BODY. (3) THE 304 DOES NOT ASSEMBLE THE DOCUMENT — counted through an instrumented store, because a 304 computed after building the body saves bandwidth and no server work. (4) a write in between makes the next conditional request return 200 with a new ETag. (5) BUMPING THE EMITTER CONSTANT ALONE INVALIDATES A CACHED PHONE with no write at all — the V3-B3(a) leg. (6) `X-Logbook-Format: 1` gets `406 unsupported_format`, and a MISSING header is treated as current.

THE URL-LEAK GUARD, REBUILT (V3-B9). v3 made 'two consecutive reads return byte-identical bodies' the primary guard and claimed 'a URL with an expiry in it fails immediately'. THAT IS FALSE: a presigned URL is a deterministic function of credentials, canonical request, `X-Amz-Date` AT ONE-SECOND GRANULARITY and expiry, so two reads in the same wall-clock second — the normal case in a Go test — produce IDENTICAL URLs. The guard was a coin flip on sub-second timing. THE DETERMINISTIC GUARDS ARE NOW PRIMARY: (a) DEC-24's own technique applied to the LOG payload — parse, walk, assert the emitted key set at EVERY level equals the golden, so a `media` or `url` key is caught BY CONSTRUCTION; (b) reject `^https?://`, protocol-relative `^//`, and any key named `url`, `expiresAt` or `signature`; (c) THE FIXTURE MUST CONTAIN AT LEAST ONE PHOTO WITH A COMMITTED ASSET, asserted as a meta-check — the plan already knows this vacuity class, having written 'the 304 leg would still pass if it were written against a log with no photographs in it'. The byte-identical leg is demoted to a smoke check. The mutation proof must redden (a) and (b), and EVIDENCE.md records which.

THE READER-SNAPSHOT LEG: a read interleaved with a trip deletion never returns a photo whose trip is absent from the same response; mutation proof drops to READ COMMITTED, run at -count=50, FAILURE RATE recorded.

*** THE SPLICE LEG (V4-B1), WHICH v4 CITED AS FIXED AND DID NOT WRITE. *** V3-B10 had two halves; v4 implemented the minor one (the ETag read inside the bump transaction) and left the primary one untouched. The primary exposure: the phone splices a returned entity into its cached document and stamps it with the server's ETag, so if its reconstruction differs from what the server would have emitted in ANY way, THE MATCHING ETAG GUARANTEES IT IS NEVER CORRECTED. THE LEG, one per non-cascading shape: perform the write, take the returned entity, splice it into the previously-cached document, then `GET /v1/logbook` and assert THE TWO DECODE TO THE SAME DOCUMENT — compared through the same emitter, NOT by raw bytes, because DEC-30 already disclaims byte stability and a byte comparison would be the same coin-flip mistake V3-B9 killed. MUTATION PROOF: have the write handler return the REQUEST BODY rather than the re-read row, and it must redden.

AND THE TRAVELLER LEG (V4-SF2): PATCH /v1/me, refresh, assert the name survives; and a traveller with no name round-trips as `null`.

The four sharing fields are PRESERVED and writable only through the /share routes — the client makes the same separation for itself, which is why `Trip.copyWithShare` exists. steps.title: Cities and places, D2's two branches, and the statement order that decides one of them
steps.work:
PUT /v1/cities/{id} with optional attachTo doing city-insert and trip-cityIds-append in ONE tx — 'One user action, one file' — and being cascading in that case, returning the whole logbook. PUT /v1/places/{id} carries the whole ORDERED visits array with explicit ordinals. DELETE /v1/places/{id}?photos=keep|delete — REQUIRED, NO DEFAULT, because D2 makes the user choose and a defaulted server guesses which of two irreversible things somebody meant.

THE STATEMENT ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING: with `photos.place_id -> places ON DELETE SET NULL`, deleting the place FIRST clears place_id on its photographs, after which `DELETE FROM photos WHERE place_id=$1` matches nothing and the photographs SURVIVE — the exact opposite of D2's 'All N, and the notes you wrote on them'. So the delete branch deletes the photographs FIRST and only then the place. The FK carries a comment saying the SET NULL is the KEEP branch.

ADDED IN v4 (DEC-46): `coverAsset` is now an OBJECT ID, so this route validates it against a committed media object for this traveller exactly as S16 validates `asset` — `422 invalid_field, field=coverAsset`. Without it one field carries two meanings and `-sweep-media` deletes live objects.

ADDED AT v5 (V4-SF6): a visits array that DROPS a visit referenced by a photograph is REFUSED — `422 invalid_field, field=visits`. `photos.visit_id -> visits ON DELETE SET NULL` means such a body silently clears those references while the phone, told the write was non-cascading, splices the place and keeps photographs pointing at a visit that is gone. No client action shrinks a visits array today, so refusing is the honest answer to a body no caller should send; if one ever should, it becomes cascading and returns the whole logbook.
steps.acceptance_check: `?photos` absent or any other value -> 422 invalid_field, field=photos. Never a default. A PUT dropping a REFERENCED visit is refused; a PUT dropping an unreferenced one succeeds.
steps.verified_by: Legs named for D2's four promises, and one asserts EXPLICITLY that the photographs are GONE on the delete branch. Mutation proofs: default `?photos` to keep (required-parameter leg reddens); REORDER the delete branch to drop the place first ('the photographs are gone' reddens) — a two-line statement swap, and therefore reachable.
steps.commit: feat(api): cities and places, D2's two branches, and the order that makes one true

steps.title: Photos: PUT, DELETE, and a refile that validates rather than re-derives
steps.work:
PUT covers setPhotoCaption; SNOOZE IS ITS OWN BULK ROUTE (see below), AND validates that `asset` names a COMMITTED media object for this traveller — 422 invalid_field, field=asset — so a broken image is impossible rather than unlikely (DEC-38). DELETE is non-cascading: 204 + ETag. POST /refile is compound and cascading, in one transaction, mirroring refilePhoto's four rules: placeId and visitId move TOGETHER; a place the trip has not visited GAINS a visit; a place it HAS visited REUSES that occasion; the place the photograph leaves KEEPS its visit; a place in ANOTHER CITY IS REFUSED. The server does NOT re-derive the occasion — the client's reuse is POSITIONAL (`visitsOn(tripId).firstOrNull`) and Kyoto in May visits one place three times, so the body carries `{placeId, visitId, visitAt}` — RULED: THE CLIENT MINTS BOTH the visit id and its timestamp — and the server VALIDATES rather than derives, creating the visit with THAT id and THAT `at` when it does not exist, at the ordinal that keeps the place's visits in `at` DESC order. (v5 left `{placeId, visitId}` standing in this first paragraph with the ruling three paragraphs below it, and a worker reads the first sentence.)

ORDERING FIXED IN v4 (V3-B8): the committed-asset validation is reachable here because the media store and the commit route landed at S11 and S12. In v3 this step preceded them, so the validation had no positive test — and a validator that rejects EVERYTHING passes 'an uncommitted asset is refused' perfectly, which is a guard that proves nothing in the plan's own vocabulary.

*** THE BULK SNOOZE ROUTE (V4-B4), RULED. *** `POST /v1/photos/snooze` with `{photoIds:[...], until}` — ONE transaction, ONE version bump, non-cascading so it returns the affected photos plus the ETag. `snoozeUnfiledPhotos(List<String>, {required DateTime until})` commits a whole day-group in one `_commit` (logbook.dart:567, called from to_file_screen.dart:87 with `item.photoIds`), and N single-photo PUTs would be N transactions, N bumps and N ETags with a partial failure leaving the group half-snoozed — inventing a partial-failure sentence for a design system with no toast. THE MAPPING RULE IS NOW NAME AND ARITY, and this is the route that property produces.

*** THE REFILE ORDINAL (V4-B5), RULED. *** Body is `{placeId, visitId, visitAt}` — THE CLIENT MINTS BOTH id and timestamp, so DEC-33's idempotency argument needs no second treatment and the client change is one call site (M2.2). A visit CREATED by refile takes the ordinal that keeps the place's visits in `at` DESC order, AND THE WHOLE PLACE'S ORDINALS ARE REWRITTEN IN THAT TRANSACTION. Append-at-max is the obvious implementation and is wrong: the client re-sorts by `at` descending, and two readers depend on it — `visitsOn(tripId).firstOrNull`, which refile itself reads, and `lastVisited => visits.first.at`.
steps.acceptance_check: A refile across cities is refused. A repeat refile with the same visitId is a no-op success. A visitId belonging to a different trip is refused. A PUT naming an uncommitted asset is refused. AND THE POSITIVE HALF, without which the negative half cannot distinguish a working validator from a broken one: a PUT naming a COMMITTED asset SUCCEEDS. A bulk snooze of N photographs performs ONE version bump — counted, not inferred. A refile-created visit lands in `at` DESC position.
steps.verified_by:
Store legs asserting no dangling reference after each — the server-side analogue of the client's expectNoDanglingReferences. Mutation proofs: drop the cross-city guard (leg reddens); make the server pick the visit itself with an unordered SELECT and the 'three visits at one place, the client's choice is honoured' leg reddens — it needs a fixture with three visits on one trip, which Kyoto-in-May supplies.

THE ORDINAL LEG, using the fixture that already exists for it — Kyoto in May visits one place THREE times: refile a photograph in, then assert the client's `firstOrNull` and `lastVisited` would resolve to the SAME visit before and after a refresh. MUTATION PROOF: append at `max(ordinal)+1` and it reddens. THE BULK LEG: snooze eight photographs, assert one bump and eight photographs returned; mutation proof splits it into eight transactions and the bump-count assertion reddens.

steps.title: GET /l/{token} — the public read, against an envelope defined seventeen steps ago
steps.size: LARGE, and the one step where a defect is a leak
steps.work:
Three flag-dependent SQL projections emitting DEC-24's ALLOWLIST — a hand-written envelope, not the client's shape. Withheld columns never SELECTed. The raw object id is NEVER emitted; with sharePhotos ON each photo carries `media:{url,expiresAt}`, a presigned read URL minted server-side. WITH sharePhotos OFF NO URL IS MINTED AT ALL — the photos key is absent and no presign call is made. Unknown and revoked are the SAME 404 with the same work done. Rate limited on the real client address; path redacted from the access log.

ADDED IN v4: `Cache-Control: no-store, private` and `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` (DEC-51) — without them the envelope, a document carrying LIVE MEDIA CAPABILITIES, is cacheable by any intermediary and by the back-forward cache, so a viewer or a shared proxy can re-read the URLs after 'Stop sharing' for as long as the cached copy survives, which is NOT bounded by the presign lifetime and unbounds the very window DEC-44 shrank. Minting uses `S3_PRESIGN_TTL_PUBLIC` (DEC-47), which is the honest revocation window and the one D3's and H1's copy is written against.

*** THE ROW RULE (V4-B2), WHICH THE KEY-SET GUARD IS BLIND TO. *** DEC-24 enumerates KEYS; it cannot tell four places from four hundred. `places` is the one collection NOT stored against the trip — places belong to the CITY and accumulate across trips — so the projection selects places with AT LEAST ONE VISIT whose `trip_id` is this trip, and the visits inside them are filtered to this trip too. `photos` and `walks` filter on their own `trip_id`; `cities` come from `trips.city_ids`. Emit places by city instead and the page leaks every other trip's pins and every wishlist place.
steps.acceptance_check: Eight golden files, one per flag combination, each compared against docs/PUBLIC-ENVELOPE.md.
steps.verified_by:
THE GUARD IS STRUCTURAL: parse, walk, and assert the emitted key set at every level EQUALS the allowlist — which is what lets the city centre stay visible, because the assertion becomes 'the only `lat` in this document is under cities[].centre'. v1's substring version was both unsatisfiable and vacuous. FIVE MUTATION PROOFS, and the first is the best line in the plan and is kept verbatim: (1) select a coordinate column and zero it in Go instead — THE STRUCTURAL LEG MUST STILL REDDEN, because the key would still be emitted; if it does not redden the test is worthless and must be rewritten. (2) make revoked answer 410 (oracle leg reddens). (3) emit an empty photos array instead of omitting the key (absence leg reddens). (4) emit the raw object id (allowlist-equality reddens). (5) NEW IN v3 AND THE SHARPEST: mint a media URL with sharePhotos FALSE — a leg asserts the presigner was NOT CALLED, counted through an instrumented store, because a URL that is minted and then discarded has still been minted, and 'not rendered' is exactly the failure mode the brief warned about.

ADDED IN v4: (6) the two headers are present, with a mutation proof removing them. (7) the mint uses the PUBLIC TTL, not the private one — asserted on `expiresAt`, because a two-minute share page is the defect DEC-47 exists to prevent.

(8) THE LEG THE KEY-SET WALK CANNOT SUBSTITUTE FOR (V4-B2): a fixture holding a WISHLIST place and a SECOND TRIP's place in the same city, asserting NEITHER appears in the envelope — and the visits of an included place carry no other trip's notes. MUTATION PROOF: drop the visit join from the places projection — THE KEY-SET LEG STAYS GREEN and only this one reddens, which EVIDENCE.md records as the plan's clearest example of a guard that looks total and is not.

steps.title: The Dockerfile — multi-stage into scratch, with the four things scratch does not give you
steps.work: Stage 1 `FROM golang:1.26 AS build` with the DEC-09 divergence comment ON the FROM line, now doubly forced: a golang:1.22 stage could not compile a module whose floor is 1.25.0. CGO_ENABLED=0, -trimpath, -ldflags. Stage 2 `scratch`. FOUR THINGS SCRATCH LACKS: (1) NO CA CERTIFICATES — and this is now LOAD-BEARING rather than precautionary, because DEC-36 makes outbound HTTPS to the bucket a real code path; without the bundle every presigned HEAD fails with an unhelpful x509 error. (2) NO TZDATA — `import _ "time/tzdata"`, because every date here is a real date. (3) NO /etc/passwd — `USER 65532:65532`, numeric only. (4) NO SHELL — a HEALTHCHECK cannot call curl, so the binary gets a `-healthcheck` flag that dials itself.
steps.acceptance_check: docker build succeeds; `docker run --rm travellog -healthcheck` behaves; the image holds the binary and the cert bundle and nothing else.
steps.verified_by: docker image inspect for layers and size; a run showing the numeric user; a container with TZ set to a NAMED zone round-tripping a date (which is what proves the tzdata import, and which fails silently without it); and a presigned HEAD against MinIO over TLS from inside the scratch image, which is what proves the CA bundle.

steps.title: docker-compose.yml, the Caddyfile, MinIO, and the two deferred addresses
steps.work:
FOUR services — DIVERGENCE 3 (DEC-39), a SPEC divergence unlike DEC-27, with a comment on the minio service naming spec L32. api, db (pinned postgres:17, named volume `pgdata`), caddy (caddy_data + caddy_config, without which automatic HTTPS re-issues on every restart into a rate limit), minio (its own named volume). Caddy takes its site address from an env var; local runs use an internal block with issuance off. Caddy sets X-Forwarded-For and its network is what TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS names; the Caddyfile omits the request URI for `/l/`. THE DB AND BUCKET PORTS ARE NOT PUBLISHED except as DEF-01/DEF-02 require.

THIS IS WHERE DEF-01 AND DEF-02 ARE ANSWERED, and only here: which hostname a physical iPhone uses, whether Caddy serves a certificate the device trusts or ATS is relaxed for development, and which address the bucket is reached at. Because of DEC-42 the answer is `.env` plus a Caddyfile site address — set `S3_PUBLIC_BASE_URL` to whatever the device can reach and `S3_INTERNAL_ENDPOINT` to the compose service, and no Go code changes. Record the answers in DEFERRED.md as resolved, with the date.
steps.acceptance_check: `docker compose config` parses; four services; `pgdata` and the minio volume are named volumes; TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS matches the compose network. DIVERGENCES.md's third entry states plainly that the fourth service is LOCAL ONLY and that a deploy against real S3 has exactly three.
steps.verified_by: `docker compose up`, `curl localhost/healthz` through Caddy, then `docker compose down && docker compose up` and assert the traveller AND the seeded media objects from the first run are BOTH still there — the only thing that proves either named volume, and the failure that hides until a redeploy. Plus: two curls with different X-Forwarded-For through Caddy get separate buckets. Plus THE DEC-42 LEG END TO END: set S3_PUBLIC_BASE_URL to the LAN address, mint a read URL, and fetch it from a different host on the network — which is the whole point of the seam and cannot be tested any earlier.

risks.risk: NEW, and it is the sharpest thing in v4: `PresignedPutObject` and `Presign` both FAIL OPEN. Reach for either and no checksum is signed, the upload succeeds, the commit HEAD succeeds because the size matches, and the object at address sha256(X) contains Y.
risks.mitigation: A grep that CAN fail (`PresignedPutObject|\.Presign(` returns nothing), the checksum leg against a PINNED MinIO tag as the mutation proof, and the ban stated in S11's work text in capitals. The second door — `Presign` — was measured in v4 and was not in the critique, which named only the first.

risks.risk: NEW, from DEC-49's emitter version: it is bumped BY HAND, so a worker who changes the emitter and forgets leaves every cached phone on the old shape.
risks.mitigation: The constant sits immediately above the emitter with a comment saying what it is for, and a leg asserts it appears in the ETag. That catches deletion, not forgetfulness — so this is a REAL residual and it is named. The alternative, hashing the emitter's output shape at init, was considered and declined as more machinery than a project of this size should carry for a constant that changes a handful of times.

risks.risk: NEW, from DEC-47's two TTLs: the public window is now the honest revocation window, and it is longer than the private one by design — so 'Stop sharing' takes longer to bite on a shared page than on the phone.
risks.mitigation: That is the trade, made explicit rather than discovered: a two-minute public window makes a share page unreadable below the fold, and the plan builds no page to re-mint from. D3's and H1's copy is written against the PUBLIC value, which DEC-35 says where the designer will read it. DEC-51's `no-store` is what stops the window being unbounded by intermediary caching, which is a different and worse failure that v3 had no guard against at all.

DEC-31 depends on the ORDER OF MAGNITUDE and is unaffected, which is why the plan was right to say so — but a figure quoted in four documents is worth being right, and three critics had recorded it as unverifiable. risks.risk: CARRIED and now guarded deterministically: a presigned URL leaking into the log payload kills the cache while nothing looks broken.

The structural key-set walk (DEC-24's technique applied to the log payload) is now primary, `^//` and the three key names are rejected alongside `^https?://`, and the fixture is asserted non-empty of photos so the leg cannot pass vacuously. risks.risk: NEW AND CLIENT-FACING (V3-SF4), and neither the plan nor the first critique raised it: on a first run with no cache, `LogbookStore.load()` returns `buildSampleLog()` — six trips about Japan — so the phone paints a full log the user never made and the background refresh then replaces it with the server's EMPTY log. The user watches their log vanish. That is the same 'stranger's data' objection the client already made for the quarantine path, arriving on the ordinary path. And `LogbookSource`'s four states no longer mean what the four screens reading them believe: `fresh` no longer means 'you have not started' and `restored` no longer means 'this is your record'.
risks.mitigation: THREE entries in CLIENT-PREREQUISITES, in the same class as DEC-35 and to be done in the same pass — and the third is the one v5 claimed and did not write (V4-SF7): DROPPING THE SEED TAKES THE CLOCK WITH IT. `logbookNowProvider` is pinned to `sampleClock` because of the fixture's dates, `main_test.dart` asserts the override list, and 34 test files pin the clock. Then: the fixture seed must go (a first run with no cache is an EMPTY log, not the sample), and `LogbookSource` needs re-specifying for the cache model — at minimum a `neverFetched` state so a first frame can say 'fetching your log' rather than 'you have not started one'. NOTE this is the one place a loading-ish state genuinely is needed, and it is at the cold-start boundary only — it does not reopen DEC-31, because `logbookProvider` still reads a file before the first frame.

vertical_slice.boundary: When the slice is checked in, the remaining plan is RE-PLANNED with the slice as `entry_state`. It is NOT resumed. Anything the slice contradicts is struck and the contradiction recorded; anything it validates is inherited.
